summary: The Safer Rail Crossing Act of 2026 requires the Secretary of Transportation to issue guidance within one year on the types of state projects that may use set-aside federal highway funds to reduce trespassing fatalities at rail crossings.

scores.thoughts: The bill directs the Secretary of Transportation to issue guidance on the use of already-set-aside funds under 23 U.S.C. § 130(e)(1)(A) for rail-crossing safety projects. It neither authorizes new appropriations nor rescinds existing funding, so it has no net effect on the overall level of government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.
No provisions address health insurance, medical services, or public-health programs.
No provisions relate to firearms regulation or Second Amendment rights.
No provisions address immigration policy, visas, border security, or enforcement.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.
No provisions affect military or defense budgets or programs.
The bill focuses exclusively on reducing trespassing fatalities at rail crossings; it does not alter environmental regulations or protections.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net benefits.
No provisions address schools, school choice, or federal education funding.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance-abuse programs.
While the bill concerns trespassing fatalities, it addresses infrastructure safety projects rather than sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
The bill does not authorize new spending or alter revenue, so it has no direct bearing on deficit or debt reduction strategies.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions relate to foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions address voting access, election administration, or voter-ID requirements.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance.
No provisions address union rights, worker protections, or employer obligations.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination protections.
